subject: maths
title: Tens and Ones: Partition Two-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Year 1 Tens and Ones Worksheets: MAB, Partitioning and Comparing, Free with Answer Key
standard_text: Partition one- and two-digit numbers in different ways using physical and virtual materials, including partitioning two-digit numbers into tens and ones
meta_desc: Free Year 1 tens and ones maths worksheets for the Australian Curriculum: count MAB longs and minis and bundles of sticks, write the number, what each digit means, partition numbers in different ways (34 = 30 + 4 = 20 + 14) and compare two-digit numbers. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: 10 ones make 1 ten. In a two-digit number, the first digit is the tens and the last digit is the ones.
key_sub: 46 is 4 tens and 6 ones, so 46 = 40 + 6, not 4 + 6. You can also break a ten: 34 = 30 + 4 = 20 + 14.
body_html:
10 ones make 1 ten

Put 10 ones together. Now you have a bundle. We call it a ten.

MAB: longs and minis

In class you use MAB. A long is 1 ten. A mini is 1 one. Count the longs by tens. Then count on the minis.

Tens and ones in a number

A two-digit number has two places. The first digit tells the tens. The last digit tells the ones.

What does the digit mean?

What does the 4 in 46 mean?

The 4 is first. It is in the tens place.

Answer: 4 tens, or 40

Partition in different ways

To partition means to split a number into parts. You can break 1 ten into 10 ones. The number stays the same.

Another way

34 = 20 + ☐

Break 1 ten into 10 ones. 3 tens and 4 ones becomes 2 tens and 14 ones.

Answer: 14, so 34 = 20 + 14

Compare two-digit numbers

Look at the tens first. More tens means a bigger number. If the tens are the same, look at the ones.

Which is more?

Which is more, 46 or 64?

46 has 4 tens. 64 has 6 tens. 6 tens is more than 4 tens.

Answer: 64

Same tens

Which is more, 52 or 57?

Both have 5 tens. Look at the ones: 7 ones is more than 2 ones.

Answer: 57

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the digits (46 = 4 + 6 = 10)The 4 is 4 tens: 46 = 40 + 6
Swapping tens and ones (4 tens and 6 ones as 64)Tens come first: 46
Writing “forty-six” as 406Use only 2 digits: 46
Counting a long as 1 (4 longs and 6 minis as 10)Each long is 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, then 41 to 46
Looking at the ones first (39 is more than 41)Look at the tens first: 41 is more than 39

faq.q: What do Year 1 students learn about tens and ones in Australia?
faq.a: The Australian Curriculum (AC9M1N02) asks Year 1 students to partition one- and two-digit numbers in different ways, including into tens and ones. For example, 34 is 3 tens and 4 ones, 30 + 4, or 20 + 14.

faq.q: What are MAB in Year 1 maths?
faq.a: MAB (multi-base arithmetic blocks) are the base-ten blocks used in Australian classrooms. A long is 10 and a mini is 1, so 4 longs and 6 minis make 46.

faq.q: What does partition mean in Year 1 maths?
faq.a: To partition is to split a number into parts. 46 can be split into 40 and 6, or into 30 and 16, and it is still 46.

faq.q: Why does my child write 64 for 46?
faq.a: They mix up which digit shows the tens. Build the number with 4 bundles of 10 and 6 loose sticks, then say “4 tens first, then 6 ones” as they write 46.
